clue.text: Accommodation for painters in the past, possibly'?

indicators.note: the painters are placed inside the shuffled letters of the next word
possibly signals that the letters of past are to be rearranged

parts.note: painters are art men, people who make art

explanation.surface: A question about where artists of bygone days used to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PAST into A-P-T-S around ART MEN; 'in' puts ART MEN between the P and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Flats or suites of rooms are places of lodging, which is what accommodation means.

clue.text: Garden fertilizer turns up in a little Dickensian work

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Some gardening dust seems to appear in a short Dickens piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses NELL + OP as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants are fertilized when this dust from the stamens reaches them, so it is literally a fertilizing agent in the garden.

clue.text: Striking finish in Mr Midshipman Easy, perhaps

definitions.text: Striking finish in Mr Midshipman Easy, perhaps

parts.words: Striking finish in Mr Midshipman Easy, perhaps
parts.note: Marryat's naval novel Mr Midshipman Easy is full of boys being flogged, and the tail of a line was the sailor's whip

explanation.surface: A remark on a dramatic ending to a seafaring novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The frayed tail of a line was used on ships to beat sailors, so it is something striking at the end.

clue.text: Clay has a change each summer

indicators.note: the words that follow undergo a change, that is, their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark that clay soil alters with every summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepiolite, the soft white mineral pipes are carved from, is often called a clay.

clue.text: An inspiring opening

explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two holes in the nose is an opening through which a person draws breath.

clue.text: Slave of 24, say

parts.note: the answer to 24 down is the foam of breaking waves

explanation.definitionFit: A medieval labourer bound to the land and its lord was effectively a slave.

clue.text: Cripples from island put up in Norfolk town

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Injured people coming from an island are lodged in an East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county in East Anglia; in a down clue 'put up' means written upward, and 'in' sets the turned island inside the town.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate or maim is to cripple someone, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Family man holds up letters for national assembly

explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' reads as one phrase meaning delays, but 'holds' is the container and 'up' turns the letters, as this is a down clue.

clue.text: Woman-age about fifty-six

clue.text: Footwear for possible hospital cases ?

explanation.definitionFit: Soft house shoes are footwear, and people who lose their footing could become hospital cases.

clue.text: Welsh river bird on ship's stern

parts.note: the Taff flows through Cardiff in Wales
a rail is a wading marsh bird

explanation.surface: A bird from a Welsh river perches at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail running round a vessel's stern is the part of the ship named.

explanation.definitionFit: Dean W. R. Inge of St Paul's was a famous Anglican cleric and columnist.

clue.text: Resident worker appears dressed as a monk

a worker is a classic crossword ant, the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: A worker in residence turns up wearing monastic clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in a place is a dweller, a resident there.

clue.text: Fur needed — cold in the country

a chill is a cold

clue.text: Cutter passes a Welsh head

indicators.note: the head of the word Welsh is its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held toothed saw is a tool that cuts.

clue.text: Mark's next-door neighbour a mean spinster

an unmarried woman is addressed as Miss

explanation.definitionFit: A shot that just fails to hit the target lands right beside the mark.

clue.text: Rite arranged by eccentric set in Italy

eccentric means the letters of set are made odd, put out of order
